task_description:
# Evolve a Polymorphic Product Catalog on Gel 6 (CLI + SDL + migrations)

## Background

This container runs a local **Gel 6** server (the graph-relational database formerly known as EdgeDB) together with the `gel` CLI. An e-commerce catalog project already exists at `/home/user/catalog`: its schema lives in `/home/user/catalog/dbschema`, two migrations have already been created and applied to the `main` branch of the local instance, and the branch already holds **12 product rows** of real data.

The current model is far too weak: prices and stock are unconstrained, the product title is a single free-form string, physical goods and digital goods cannot be told apart, and nothing prevents duplicate listings. Your job is to redesign the model, migrate the **already-populated** database to it **without losing or corrupting a single existing row**, add the missing catalog data, and ship a deterministic reporting command that exercises the new polymorphic model.

## Requirements

### 1. Target schema (module `default`)

Two custom scalar types:

- `Sku`, derived from `str`, that accepts only values matching the regular expression `^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}$`.
- `ListingStatus`, an enumerated scalar whose values are exactly, in this order: `draft`, `active`, `archived`.

An **abstract** object type `Product` carrying:

- `sku`: required, of type `Sku`, unique across the whole catalog.
- `brand`: required `str`.
- `name`: required `str`.
- `title`: a computed single `str` equal to `brand`, then the exact three characters ` | ` (space, vertical bar, space), then `name`. It must be computed, not stored.
- `price_cents`: required `int64` that may never be smaller than 1.
- `discount_cents`: required `int64` that may never be negative and that defaults to 0 for newly inserted products.
- `final_price_cents`: a computed single `int64` equal to `price_cents` minus `discount_cents`.
- `units_in_stock`: required `int64` that may never be negative. This is the property currently called `stock`, and its stored values must survive the migration; afterwards no property named `stock` may remain anywhere in the model.
- `listing_status`: required `ListingStatus`, with **no** default value.
- A type-level rule that rejects any product whose `discount_cents` is greater than its `price_cents`.
- A type-level uniqueness rule over the pair (`brand`, `name`) that is enforced across the entire catalog, regardless of the concrete product type.
- `accessories`: a `multi` link to `Product` carrying a **required** link property `rank` of type `int16`, plus a rule that forbids one product from having two accessories with the same `rank`.
- `accessory_of`: a computed `multi` backlink exposing the products that list this product among their accessories.
- An index on the `brand` property, and a composite index on the pair (`listing_status`, `price_cents`) in that order. No index over the old `title` expression may survive.

Three concrete object types extending `Product`:

- `Book`: required `author: str`, optional `pages: int64`.
- `Apparel`: required `size_label: str`.
- `DigitalDownload` (new): required `file_size_kb: int64` that may never be smaller than 1.

### 2. Data-preserving evolution of the populated branch

- All 12 pre-existing products must still exist afterwards, each keeping the **same `id`** and the same `sku` as recorded in `/opt/task/initial_state.json`, the same concrete type, the same `price_cents`, the same subtype-specific values (`author`, `pages`, `size_label`), and a `units_in_stock` equal to its former `stock`.
- `brand` and `name` of each pre-existing product must be derived from its former `title`, split at the ` | ` separator, so that the new computed `title` is byte-identical to the former `title`.
- `listing_status` of a pre-existing product must be `active` when its stock was greater than 0 and `archived` otherwise. No pre-existing product may end up as `draft`.
- `discount_cents` must be 0 for every pre-existing product.
- The migration history must stay healthy: `gel migration status` must report that the branch is in sync with `/home/user/catalog/dbschema`; the two already-applied migrations must remain in the recorded history untouched (do not squash, rewrite, renumber or delete them); at least one new migration must be added; and the number of `.edgeql` files under `/home/user/catalog/dbschema/migrations` must equal the number of migrations recorded in the database.

### 3. Catalog data to add

Insert exactly two new products, both `DigitalDownload`, and no other new products:

| sku | brand | name | price_cents | discount_cents | units_in_stock | listing_status | file_size_kb |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DLD-0001` | `Northwind` | `Trail Guide PDF` | 1200 | 200 | 999 | `active` | 8200 |
| `DLD-0002` | `Cobalt` | `Layering Course` | 4900 | 0 | 500 | `draft` | 152000 |

Wire up accessories exactly like this and nowhere else in the catalog:

- the product with sku `BOK-0001` has two accessories: `DLD-0001` with `rank` 1 and `APP-0005` with `rank` 2;
- the product with sku `APP-0001` has one accessory: `APP-0005` with `rank` 1.

### 4. Reporting command

Provide an executable command at `/home/user/catalog/bin/catalog-report` that takes no arguments, queries the **live** database every time it runs, prints a single JSON document to stdout, and exits with code 0. It must never modify the database, and two consecutive runs must produce byte-identical output. It must not embed precomputed results: if catalog rows change, its output must change accordingly.

## Implementation Hints

- Project path: `/home/user/catalog`. Schema directory: `/home/user/catalog/dbschema` (schema files and the `migrations/` folder live there).
- The local Gel server may not be running yet. Run `gel-start` to make sure it is up; it is idempotent and exits 0 once the server accepts queries. Connection settings (host, port, TLS, branch `main`) are already exported in the environment, so `gel` commands need no connection flags.
- Do **not** run `gel project init`, `gel instance create`, `gel instance link`, `gel branch create/switch/wipe`, or `gel database wipe`, and do not create a second instance, branch or data directory: the graded database is the `main` branch of the running local instance. There is no network access.
- `/opt/task/initial_state.json` is a read-only snapshot of the database as it was handed to you (recorded migration names, and for every product its `id`, `sku`, `title`, `price_cents`, `stock`, concrete type and subtype fields). You may read it.
- Keep the dataset small; do not add products beyond the two required ones.
- Output shape of `/home/user/catalog/bin/catalog-report`: a JSON object with exactly the keys `products`, `restock_alerts` and `totals`.
  - `products` is an array holding **every** product in the catalog, sorted by `sku` in ascending byte order. Each element is an object with exactly the keys `sku`, `brand`, `name`, `title`, `kind`, `listing_status`, `price_cents`, `discount_cents`, `final_price_cents`, `units_in_stock`, `accessories` and `detail`. `kind` is the concrete type name without its module prefix (`Book`, `Apparel` or `DigitalDownload`). `listing_status` is the enum value as a string. `accessories` is an array, sorted by `rank` ascending, whose elements are objects with exactly the keys `sku` (string) and `rank` (number); it is an empty array when the product has no accessories. `detail` is an object holding exactly the subtype-specific fields of that product: `author` and `pages` for a `Book` (with `pages` being JSON `null` when it has no value), `size_label` for an `Apparel`, `file_size_kb` for a `DigitalDownload`.
  - `restock_alerts` is an array of sku strings sorted in ascending order, containing exactly the products that are **not** digital downloads, whose `listing_status` is not `archived`, and whose `units_in_stock` is strictly less than 5.
  - `totals` is an object with exactly the keys `product_count`, `book_count`, `apparel_count`, `digital_count`, `active_inventory_value_cents` and `average_active_final_price`. The first five are JSON numbers: the counts of all products and of each concrete type, and the sum of `final_price_cents` multiplied by `units_in_stock` over the products whose `listing_status` is `active` (0 when there are none). `average_active_final_price` is a JSON **string**: the arithmetic mean of `final_price_cents` over the products whose `listing_status` is `active`, rounded half-up to two decimal places and rendered with exactly two decimals, for example `1234.50`; it must be `0.00` when no product is active.
  - Every value other than `average_active_final_price`, the sku/brand/name/title/kind/listing_status strings and the string subtype fields must be a JSON number (never a numeric string).
- Constraint violations must be enforced by the database itself, so that invalid writes attempted through the `gel` CLI or any client fail with a Gel constraint-violation error instead of being silently accepted or filtered in application code.

truth:
# Verification Plan

## Setup

1. Run `gel-start` once to guarantee the local Gel server is listening (idempotent, exit code 0). Every check that shells out to the `gel` CLI or reads the database must depend on this step having run first.
2. Load the reference snapshot `/opt/task/initial_state.json` (baked into the image at build time). It contains `migrations` (the ordered names of the two migrations applied before the task started) and `products` (for each of the 12 seeded rows: `id`, `sku`, `title`, `price_cents`, `stock`, `kind`, and `author`/`pages`/`size_label` where applicable).
3. Do not delete or rewrite anything in `/home/user/catalog`. Any row the verification inserts must be deleted again in the same check.

## Verification Steps

1. **Migration history is in sync.** Run `gel migration status --quiet` with the working directory `/home/user/catalog`; expect exit code 0.
2. **History was extended, not rewritten.** Query the migrations recorded in the database (`schema::Migration`); expect both names from `initial_state.json.migrations` to still be present, the total recorded count to be at least 3, and that count to equal the number of `*.edgeql` files under `/home/user/catalog/dbschema/migrations` (resolve those files with a glob; migration filenames are content-hashed, never bare indexes).
3. **Custom scalars.** Introspect `schema::ScalarType` for `default::Sku`: it extends `std::str` and carries a regexp constraint whose argument is `^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}$`. Introspect `default::ListingStatus`: `enum_values` equals `['draft', 'active', 'archived']`.
4. **Type hierarchy.** `default::Product` is abstract; `default::Book`, `default::Apparel` and `default::DigitalDownload` all exist, are not abstract, and list `default::Product` among their ancestors.
5. **Product properties.** Introspecting `default::Product` pointers: `sku` is required with target `default::Sku`; `brand`, `name` required `std::str`; `price_cents`, `discount_cents`, `units_in_stock` required `std::int64`; `listing_status` required with target `default::ListingStatus` and no default; `title` and `final_price_cents` are computed (non-empty `expr`) while `brand`, `name`, `units_in_stock` and `listing_status` are not computed; no pointer named `stock` or `title` that is a plain stored property remains.
6. **Subtype properties.** `Book.author` required `std::str` and `Book.pages` optional `std::int64`; `Apparel.size_label` required `std::str`; `DigitalDownload.file_size_kb` required `std::int64`. Do not assert *how* the numeric bounds are expressed (any constraint flavour is acceptable) — the numeric bounds are graded behaviourally by the negative checks below.
7. **Structural constraints on Product.** The type-level constraints of `default::Product` include a `std::exclusive` whose subject expression mentions both `brand` and `name`, and a `std::expression` whose expression (concatenate `expr`, `subjectexpr` and `finalexpr` before matching) mentions both `discount_cents` and `price_cents`; the `sku` pointer carries `std::exclusive`; `listing_status` has an empty `default`; `discount_cents` has a non-empty `default`.
8. **Indexes.** The index expressions declared on `default::Product` (with whitespace removed) include `.brand` (or `(.brand)`) and one that starts with `(` and mentions `.listing_status` before `.price_cents`; none of them mentions `title`.
9. **Link and link property.** On `default::Product`, `accessories` is a link with cardinality `Many` and target `default::Product`; drilling into it with an explicit `[is schema::Link]` type intersection (a plain nested `pointers` shape fails on `schema::Pointer`), it owns a pointer `rank` that is required with target `std::int16`, and it carries a `std::exclusive` constraint whose subject expression mentions `rank`. `accessory_of` is a link with a non-empty `expr` and cardinality `Many`.
10. **Seeded rows preserved.** For every product in the snapshot, a product with the same `id` still exists and has the same `sku`, the same `kind` (`__type__.name` without the module prefix), the same `price_cents`, `units_in_stock` equal to the snapshot `stock`, and the same subtype fields (`author`/`pages`/`size_label`). Total product count is exactly 14.
11. **Title split preserved.** For every seeded product, the live computed `title` equals the snapshot `title`, `brand` equals the part before the first ` | ` and `name` equals the part after it.
12. **Backfilled listing_status.** For every seeded product, `listing_status` is `active` when the snapshot `stock` is greater than 0 and `archived` otherwise, and no seeded product is `draft`. Cross-check the same rule against the live `units_in_stock` values.
13. **Discounts backfilled to zero.** Every seeded product has `discount_cents` equal to 0, and `final_price_cents` equals `price_cents`.
14. **New digital rows.** Exactly two `DigitalDownload` rows exist, with skus `DLD-0001` and `DLD-0002` and exactly the brand/name/price_cents/discount_cents/units_in_stock/listing_status/file_size_kb values given in the task description; their computed `title` values are `Northwind | Trail Guide PDF` and `Cobalt | Layering Course`.
15. **Accessory wiring.** `BOK-0001` links `DLD-0001` at rank 1 and `APP-0005` at rank 2; `APP-0001` links `APP-0005` at rank 1; the total number of accessory links in the catalog is 3; `APP-0005` reports `BOK-0001` and `APP-0001` through the computed `accessory_of` backlink.
16. **Report command runs and is deterministic.** `/home/user/catalog/bin/catalog-report` exists and is executable; running it with no arguments exits 0 and prints parseable JSON; two consecutive runs print byte-identical stdout; the top-level keys are exactly `products`, `restock_alerts`, `totals`; running it does not change the number of products.
17. **Report products match the live database.** Independently query all products (sku, brand, name, title, concrete type, listing_status, price_cents, discount_cents, final_price_cents, units_in_stock, accessories with their rank, and subtype fields) and compare, element by element, with the `products` array of the report, including the ascending `sku` ordering, the exact per-element key sets, the `kind` values without module prefix, the accessory ordering by rank, `null` for a missing `pages`, and that every numeric field is a JSON number.
18. **Report totals match the live database.** Recompute `product_count`, `book_count`, `apparel_count`, `digital_count` and `active_inventory_value_cents` from live queries and compare with `totals`; recompute `average_active_final_price` from the live active `final_price_cents` values using half-up rounding to two decimals formatted with exactly two decimals and compare the string.
19. **Report restock alerts match the live database.** Recompute the expected sku list from live data using a type-intersection query (products that are not `DigitalDownload`, `listing_status` not `archived`, `units_in_stock` < 5), sorted ascending, and compare with `restock_alerts`. With the required data this list is `['APP-0001', 'APP-0004', 'APP-0006', 'BOK-0003']`.
20. **Report reacts to live data (anti-hardcoding).** Insert a fresh `Book` with a randomly generated sku matching `^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}$` (retrying/choosing so that it does not collide), a random unique brand/name pair, `price_cents` 5000, `units_in_stock` 2, `listing_status` `active` and **no** `discount_cents` at all; expect the row to be stored with `discount_cents` 0 and `final_price_cents` 5000, and its computed `title` to be the brand, ` | ` and the name. Re-run the report and expect `products` to contain the new sku with the correct `kind` `Book` and `detail.pages` equal to JSON `null`, `totals.product_count` to have grown by one, `totals.book_count` to have grown by one, and `restock_alerts` to contain the new sku; then delete the inserted row and re-run the report to confirm it disappears again and `product_count` is back to 14.
21. **Negative: duplicate sku.** Inserting a `Book` reusing an existing sku fails with a non-zero exit status and a `ConstraintViolationError`.
22. **Negative: malformed sku.** Inserting a `Book` whose sku is `bad-sku` fails with `ConstraintViolationError`.
23. **Negative: duplicate brand/name pair.** Inserting an `Apparel` reusing the `brand` and `name` of an existing `Book` (read live from the database) fails with `ConstraintViolationError`.
24. **Negative: discount above price.** Inserting a valid-looking `Book` with `price_cents` 1000 and `discount_cents` 1001 fails with `ConstraintViolationError`.
25. **Negative: non-positive price and negative stock.** Inserting a `Book` with `price_cents` 0 fails with `ConstraintViolationError`; inserting a `Book` with `units_in_stock` -1 fails with `ConstraintViolationError`.
26. **Negative: missing required listing_status.** Inserting a `Book` that omits `listing_status` fails with a `MissingRequiredError`.
27. **Negative: undersized digital download.** Inserting a `DigitalDownload` with `file_size_kb` 0 fails with `ConstraintViolationError`.
28. **Negative: duplicate accessory rank.** Adding another accessory to `BOK-0001` with `rank` 1 fails with `ConstraintViolationError`.
29. After every negative check, confirm the total product count is still 14 and no stray row survived.
